title: Fall of Constantinople
summary: The Ottoman siege that ended a thousand years of Byzantine rule and opened a new chapter in the struggle for the eastern Mediterranean.

stories.title: The Siege of 1453
stories.summary: Mehmed II's fifty-three-day assault on the last great Christian city of the East.

events.title: Ottoman blockade
events.body: Sultan Mehmed II encircled Constantinople with an army estimated at eighty thousand men. The Theodosian Walls had never fallen to a direct assault — but the Ottomans intended to break that record.

events.title: Bombardment
events.body: Mehmed deployed massive bronze cannon — including the legendary Basilica — to batter the land walls day after day. Sections crumbled under the bombardment, forcing the defenders into constant repair.

events.title: Chain across Golden Horn
events.body: A massive chain blocked the Golden Horn, keeping Ottoman galleys out of the harbour. Mehmed countered by hauling ships overland on greased rollers into the inlet — a manoeuvre that stunned the defenders.

events.title: Final assault
events.body: After weeks of attrition, Mehmed launched a massive final assault before dawn. Janissaries and irregulars poured through a breach in the walls as Byzantine resistance finally collapsed.

events.title: Fall of the city
events.body: Constantine XI died fighting at the walls. Hagia Sophia became a mosque, and the Byzantine Empire — heir to Rome — was extinguished. Istanbul would serve as the Ottoman capital for centuries.

stories.title: Rise of the Ottomans
stories.summary: From a frontier beylik to a Mediterranean power.
